Class SlotScroll

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.SlotScroll
public final class SlotScroll extends Object
A grid of slots that scrolls inside its panel when it doesn't fit (7.4.0): as tall as its live rows while there is room, shorter by whole rows when there isn't, never under its minimum rows, scrolling past what shows. The slots are a slot library's elements (SlotKit's SlotElement, one per cell); MenuKit names no slot type, so each cell is made by the consumer from its index and its place. 
PanelElement grid = SlotScroll.builder()
        .cells(27, (i, x, y, shown) -> mySlot(i, x, y, shown))   // SlotElement.builder().slot(id, i).at(x, y).visibleWhen(shown).build()
        .build();

Sizing

It is a ScrollContainer that fits the room (ScrollContainer.Builder.fitRoom(int)) in whole rows: in a ContainerRegion section the region asks it to give back what the list would overflow the screen by, so it shows every live row and no scrollbar while the window has the height, and scrolls once it is too short. Elsewhere nothing asks, and it is as tall as its live rows. Never under SlotScroll.Builder.minRows rows, so a box with fewer live slots keeps a chest's height and the frame holds still as its rows change.

Narrowing or a lane outside

A grid that may narrow (SlotScroll.Builder.narrows(), a bundle) drops to one column fewer while it scrolls, so those columns and the scrollbar fill the grid's width and the panel never widens for it. One that must keep its columns (a chest) has the scrollbar's lane beside it while it scrolls (ScrollContainer.Builder.laneOutside), and the region widens its frame by as much. Fewer columns are more rows, so once narrowed a grid stays narrowed until the narrow grid fits.

Live slots

Only the first live cells show, so the scroll ends at the last live row. Without a live count, it is the leading cells that are visible on their own (a slot library's element hides itself where its slot isn't on the menu). Either is read before the screen lays out, once at each of its inits and once a frame while the grid is on screen, never per cell: layout asks for the grid's height many times a frame. A live count that throws counts as none live, and is logged once.

Flat cells

Each cell is placed at its own place straight in the scroll area, not in rows of their own: a nested row makes layout measure every cell many times a frame. A narrowing grid has a second set placed a column fewer a row, one set shown at a time. A slot library's group element (one element drawing many slots) draws nothing inside a scroll area; give one element per cell.

A shift-click lands in view

A quick move into one of its slots scrolled out of view scrolls the grid there, as the container region does for its own rows. A slot the grid hasn't drawn yet is looked for a viewport at a time, and the grid goes back to where it was if no page has it.

ScrollContainer.scrolls() says whether it scrolls now: where a mod would do something else with the wheel over it (switch tabs), the wheel is the grid's while it scrolls. In the container region ContainerRegion.scrolls(screen) already counts a section's grid.
